Second Derivatives of a Score-Driven Predictor

Source: R/gas.R
term_curvature.GasTerm.Rd

Computes the forward Jacobian of the filter's predictor in a caller's unknowns and the second derivative contracted against the caller's weights, and propagates both through the recursion beside the state.

Arguments

term

A built GasTerm.

eta

The static part of the predictor.

y

The response, unused directly.

score, curvature

The callbacks of term_filter().

psi

The parameters on the parameter scale, named as term_params().

g

The weights against which the second derivative is contracted.

seed

The derivative of the static predictor in the unknowns.

blocks

The model's own derivative pieces; see term_curvature().

...

Unused.

score_values, curvature_values

The score and curvature of the model's log-density evaluated at the current predictors, one value per observation, on the parameter scale that the callbacks read. Supplying both, together with blocks_data, routes the recursion through the compiled kernel, on the route without subformulas as well as on the route with them. If any of the three is NULL, the R route runs.

blocks_data

The model's derivative pieces as data instead of as a callback: a list with H (the mixed second derivatives, one column per distribution parameter), D3 (the third derivatives with the filter's own parameter as first index, one column per pair of the other two indices, pair (r, r2) at column (r - 1) * n_par + r2, with n_par the number of distribution parameters), Vs (the per-parameter jacobian rows of the other equations) and ap (the filter's own parameter index), and for the third and fourth orders D4 and D5, one column per index triple and quadruple after the filter's own, laid out the same way. Only the compiled route reads it.

threads

Threads for the compiled route's group loop, as numericals7::n_threads() counts them; 1 is sequential.

Value

A list with jacobian and curvature.

Details

With subformulas the general per-observation route runs instead, and the second derivative is accumulated on each group's active set rather than as a square over all the unknowns: a development's coordinate reaches only the groups where its column is not identically zero, so with grouping indicators the active set has the same size whether the panel has ten groups or a thousand. Accumulating the square over all the unknowns would grow with the square of their number, and the number of unknowns grows with the number of groups.

blocks is called as blocks(e, i, v, act), where v is the row of the Jacobian restricted to the active set act, and returns its pieces in the coordinates of that set. A callback of three arguments, blocks(e, i, v), is also accepted: it is given the full row and its result is subset here, which costs the quadratic allocation that the restriction is meant to avoid.
